cells.value: National farmer registry EXISTS and is OPERATING: the MALR 'Farmer Card' (كارت الفلاح) smart-card system is the national electronic agricultural holding registry. MALR spokesperson (via SIS, 28 Mar 2026): ~5 million farmers have benefited from the system, which tracks subsidised fertiliser distribution directly. MALR (SIS, 8 May 2026): summer-2026 fertiliser disbursement runs through the Farmer Card system at all agricultural cooperatives nationwide. Earlier official milestone (MALR press conference, 6 Dec 2021): >3.5m cards printed, 2m distributed, Meeza payment feature being added. Press-reported (T5, not load-bearing): 5.6m holdings registered = 94% of book holdings (ministry statement, May 2024); 4.8m farmers registered (Minister of Agriculture, Jan 2026); 3.7m cards issued by Agricultural Bank of Egypt (Jul 2026).
cells.source_title: SIS (State Information Service): 'Agriculture spokesperson: continued efforts to ensure support reaches farmers through the Farmer Card' [Arabic], 28 March 2026
cells.quality_evidence: Institutionalised: card is the mandatory channel for subsidised fertiliser nationwide (SIS 8 May 2026, T3: disbursement 'through the Farmer Card system' at all agricultural cooperatives, with >5,500 electronic POS machines per press reports); payments integration with Meeza announced by Minister (SIS Story 201846) and confirmed in MALR Dec-2021 press conference ('payments feature being added to the card'); registry records name, ID, landholding, crops, quota and underpins subsidy targeting. Programme dates to a Nov-2016 contract (per Xinhua/al-ain, T5) with rollout from ~2019.
cells.scale_evidence: T3: ~5 million farmer beneficiaries (SIS, 28 Mar 2026, source MENA agency). T3 (dated): >3.5m cards printed / 2m distributed (MALR, 6 Dec 2021). T5-flagged: 5.6m holdings = 94% of book holdings (ministry statement May 2024, carried by Tridge/Bashaier); 4.8m farmers registered (Youm7 quoting Minister, Jan 2026); 3.7m cards issued (ABE via Masrawy, Jul 2026). Denominator (total farm households/holdings) not verified from a current census source — the ministry's own coverage metric is '94% of book holdings'.
cells.search_trail: Searched: SIS.gov.eg (site: search, Arabic + English), moa.gov.eg news pages (fetched via curl, resolve HTTP 200), FAO (no Egypt farmer-registry report found), RFILC 'Transforming Agriculture through Digital Farmer Registries' policy brief Jan 2026 (PDF downloaded, zero Egypt mentions), Arabic press for current counts (Youm7/Dostor/Masrawy/al-ain, T5, corroboration only). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Scale figures circulate in three non-comparable units (cards issued, farmers registered, holdings registered) with no official time series; the only T3-quoted current figure is 'about 5 million farmers benefited'. sis.gov.eg presents a TLS certificate WebFetch rejects ('unable to verify the first certificate'); content verified via curl -k. Recommend Wayback capture of the SIS/MALR deep links.
cells.notes: PREREQUISITE FIN+AGI cell. Prior desk-pass lead ('MALR Farmer Card / Meeza system since 2016') VERIFIED as Operating; counts updated from unspecified to T3-sourced ~5m beneficiaries (2026). Divergences from prior: prior gave no farmer count; prior's '(since 2016)' refers to the Nov-2016 build contract (T5), with operational rollout from ~2019-2021. Egypt lead only — the Nigeria lead in the shared guidance is out of scope for this Egypt bundle.

cells.value: Digital land registration is ADOPTED but not yet a comprehensive operating digital cadastre. New: Law No. 88 of 2025 (signed 18 June 2025; Official Gazette issue 24-bis, 17 June 2025) establishes a unified national electronic real-estate ID database assigning every property a unique national ID linked to Egypt's unified digital base map (SIS, T3). Baseline remains weak: the World Bank Assessment of Land Governance in Egypt (2022, T2) states 'While title registration has been applied to agricultural land, it is estimated that only 25 percent of land parcels are accurately recorded in the system', and legal property registration 'has progressively become less applicable... basically irrelevant for most urban and rural properties'. Press (T5, note only): World Bank cited in July 2026 as saying <10% of Egypt's real estate is formally registered despite the digital-ID rollout. Separately, MALR's electronic agricultural holding registry (Farmer Card, see 3.3) operates nationwide at plot/holding level for input allocation — a usufruct/holding register, not legal title.
cells.source_title: SIS: 'President El-Sisi Signs Law Establishing National Real Estate Identification Number Database' (Law 88/2025), June 2025
cells.quality_evidence: Legal basis enacted (Law 88/2025, gazetted 17 June 2025) with a mandated central electronic database and geospatial linkage to the unified base map; excludes strategic/military properties. Real Estate Publicity Department (Ministry of Justice) remains the registration authority; official realestate.gov.eg platform documents an ongoing but still largely paper-based process ('digitalization of the real estate registry system' listed as a reform in progress). WB 2022 (T2): registration regime described as 'nearly-dysfunctional'; reforms simplified documentation and dropped chain-of-title requirements.
cells.scale_evidence: Agricultural land: only ~25% of parcels accurately recorded in the title registration system (WB Assessment of Land Governance in Egypt, 2022 — quote verified in full text). Overall property registration <10% (World Bank figure as reported by Daily News Egypt, 5 July 2026 — T5 carrier, flagged). National real-estate ID database: implementation phase, no published enrolment counts found.
cells.search_trail: Searched: World Bank documents (Assessment of Land Governance in Egypt — full text downloaded and quote verified), SIS.gov.eg (Law 88/2025 signing), realestate.gov.eg official platform blog, law-firm summaries (ADSERO, Riad&Riad — T5, corroboration), Daily News Egypt (T5), Land Portal/GLTN. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: The WB 25% figure's underlying observation predates the 2022 report (report synthesis; no primary survey year given) — recorded as 2022 report-year evidence. The <10% overall registration figure is attributed to the World Bank only via a T5 news carrier; primary WB 2026 source not located this pass.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior desk pass: prior cited 'Ministry of Justice / ESA cadastre modernization; Ahram Online' and a 'Nationwide Title Cadastre System since ~2005' — the ~2005 NTCS claim could not be re-verified this pass and is dropped; replaced with the gazetted Law 88/2025 (T3) and WB land-governance quantification (T2). Prior's overall characterisation (long-running, incomplete digitisation) stands.

cells.value: Open agricultural data is ADOPTED in policy but the national open-data portal is NOT yet live. Egypt's first Open Data Policy (issued by the National Council for Artificial Intelligence, 2025; prepared by MCIT; reported in force August 2025) mandates open-by-default for public-classified datasets, machine-readable open formats (CSV/JSON/XML, explicitly discouraging PDF-only), standardized bilingual metadata, a CC-BY/ODC-BY-aligned national license, and designates a National Open Data Portal at data.gov.eg as single point of access with MCIT building it — but data.gov.eg does not resolve as of 2026-08-22 (DNS check: no host). Operating partial assets: MALR Economic Affairs Sector portal (agri.gov.eg, launched 17 July 2022) publishes agricultural statistics databases (time series for crop, livestock, poultry, fish production), an interactive governorate crop map, agricultural censuses and bulletins — but bulletins are described as PDF files; Egypt Data Portal (egypt.opendataforafrica.org, AfDB-hosted, CAPMAS-populated) carries an Agriculture category with export/API. No dedicated machine-readable national agricultural open-data portal exists.
cells.source_title: Open Data Policy, Arab Republic of Egypt — issued by the National Council for Artificial Intelligence, 2025 (official PDF on ai.gov.eg)
cells.quality_evidence: Policy is a formal transitional instrument pending a Data Governance Law (explicitly 'forthcoming' in the text) and creation of an Egyptian Data Governance Authority (EDGA); governance assigned to NCAI Interagency Data Release Board with Open Data Officers per agency; MCIT named technical secretariat to 'develop the national data portal'. Policy text extracted and verified from the official PDF. MALR's own statistics portal states its vision as 'digitising Egyptian agriculture' with time-series databases (site launched 17 July 2022; >3.5m visits).
cells.scale_evidence: No dataset counts or portal usage statistics available for agricultural open data; data.gov.eg not yet live (DNS failure verified 2026-08-22, twice, both apex and www). Egypt Data Portal (AfDB/CAPMAS) agriculture category exists but is third-party-hosted and its dataset inventory was not enumerable this pass (Cloudflare JS wall).
cells.search_trail: Searched: data.gov.eg (DNS check — does not resolve), ai.gov.eg Open Data Policy PDF (downloaded, text extracted), egypt.gov.eg open-data initiative page, CAPMAS (capmas.gov.eg and censusinfo.capmas.gov.eg — both timed out from test network; existence documented via UN Statistical Commission and UNESCWA profiles), egypt.opendataforafrica.org (Cloudflare-blocked to curl; documented via UNESCWA opengov profile), agri.gov.eg (fetched, content verified), ODIN/Open Data Watch Egypt 2024 profile (JS app, scores not extractable this pass), MCIT publications. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Tier call: 'in force August 2025' comes from a T5 tech-news carrier (TechAfrica, 8 Sep 2025) quoting MCIT; the policy PDF itself (T3) is undated beyond '2025'. ODIN 2024 agriculture-category scores exist but the ODIN site is a JS application whose values could not be extracted — worth one manual pull for the next loop. CAPMAS's own portal being unreachable from a non-Egyptian network is a resolvability concern for any CAPMAS deep link.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior desk pass: prior ('sector review — no comprehensive national ag open-data portal, integration suggested by MALR/MCIT projects') is confirmed on the portal absence, but the prior MISSED the 2025 NCAI Open Data Policy — a material new T3 fact that moves this cell from vague 'sector review' to documented Adopted with a named, testable portal commitment (data.gov.eg).

cells.value: Weather/climate data infrastructure is OPERATING with ag-tailored services. The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) is the operational national met service (official site www.ema.gov.eg resolves; agrometeorology is a named EMA research/service area, and EMA cooperates with the Ministry of Agriculture on periodic reports to agricultural research bodies). MALR/ARC runs dedicated agro-climate units: the Central Laboratory for Agricultural Climate (CLAC) and the ARC Climate Change Information Center issue technical advisories to farmers for weather events — e.g., SIS-carried bulletin instructing farmers nationwide on handling an unstable-weather wave (wind/rain). The DAIRS climate early-warning system was reported 'under development' alongside government apps Al Mufeed and Hudhud (ICARDA, 'Current Situation of Digital Agriculture in Egypt', 28 Dec 2023, T2). No verified figures on farmer reach of agromet advisories.
cells.source_title: SIS: 'Agriculture issues its recommendations to farmers on dealing with the unstable weather wave in the coming days' [Arabic] (CLAC/ARC advisory)
cells.quality_evidence: Institutionalised: EMA is the statutory national meteorological authority (WMO member; own domain www.ema.gov.eg, HTTP 200 verified); CLAC and the Climate Change Information Center are permanent ARC units under MALR; advisories are issued in coordination with ARC research institutes and carried on official state channels (SIS). Heat-wave and cold-wave technical recommendations for farmers documented across seasons.
cells.scale_evidence: None found: no published figures for the share of farmers receiving agromet/climate advisories (consistent with prior gap on indicator 8.17). DAIRS (dedicated ag climate early-warning) still 'under development' per the latest verifiable source (ICARDA 2023).
cells.search_trail: Searched: EMA official domains (www.ema.gov.eg HTTP 200; en.emaeg.org and nwp.gov.eg DNS-fail from test network), arc.sci.eg CLAC page (DNS-fail — cited via SIS instead), SIS.gov.eg Arabic (CLAC/CCIC advisories found), ICARDA/CGSpace digital-agriculture review (fetched), FAO Near East early-warning forum item, WMO library. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: arc.sci.eg (ARC, home of CLAC) does not resolve from outside Egypt at capture time, so the CLAC institutional page is cited indirectly via SIS — a resolvability defect for T3 sourcing. DAIRS status evidence is from Dec 2023; anything newer is T5 only.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior desk pass: prior dated the ICARDA review as 2025 — the CGSpace item is dated 28/12/2023; DAIRS 'under development' is therefore a 2023 observation, not 2025. Prior under-reported the operating layer: EMA + CLAC/CCIC ag advisories are operational T3 facts the prior's 'DAIRS-only' framing missed.

cells.value: Satellite/EO integration in agriculture is OPERATING beyond pilots. T3 (MALR press conference, 6 Dec 2021): MALR and MCIT used AI to inventory the cropped area of each crop on the ground ('completed the summer-season crop inventory; preparing the winter-season inventory') — an operational, recurring national product. NARSS (National Authority for Remote Sensing and Space Sciences) and MALR presented the national winter 2023/24 crop map built with remote sensing + AI (Daily News Egypt, 5 Nov 2024 — T5 existence fact; NARSS is the standing national EO authority, narss.sci.eg). FAO with MWRI and MALR ran satellite crop-mapping for water accounting: 90 engineers trained, 259,000 feddans mapped across Minya, Kafr El-Sheikh and Sharqia (FAO Near East, 5 Apr 2021 — pilot/capacity phase). An AI crop-mapping and field-boundary detection solution was implemented for ARC (Esri partner announcement — T5, fetch blocked 403, flagged). No specific operational EgSA agricultural programme verified this pass.
cells.source_title: MALR: 'Ministers of Agriculture and Communications announce pilot launch of digital transformation services in the agricultural sector' [Arabic], 6 December 2021 (includes completed AI crop-area inventory)
cells.quality_evidence: Multi-agency institutional base: MALR-MCIT joint programme (T3, 2021, verified page text); NARSS is the permanent national remote-sensing authority coordinating strategic-crop inventory with MALR (winter 2023/24 map presented Nov 2024); peer-reviewed Egyptian crop-mapping literature is extensive (Sentinel/Landsat wheat and rice mapping, Nile Delta). FAO/Sida water-accounting crop maps add an irrigation-management use case with MWRI.
cells.scale_evidence: National seasonal crop inventories claimed complete for summer season and recurring (T3, 2021; winter 2023/24 map presented 2024). Quantified pilot coverage: 259,000 feddans across 3 governorates (FAO, 2021). No published accuracy/coverage statistics for the national inventory located this pass.
cells.search_trail: Searched: moa.gov.eg highlights (fetched, text verified), agri.gov.eg news (item 19237 not directly renderable — JS/topic page), SIS.gov.eg AI+satellite items, FAO Near East (fetched), NARSS (narss.sci.eg indexed; site not deep-fetched), Esri newsroom (403), Daily News Egypt Nov 2024 (T5), peer-reviewed crop-mapping literature (ScienceDirect/MDPI). Access date 2026-08-22.

cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior desk pass: same substantive finding (operational satellite/AI crop mapping, level-4-type facts), but the prior's citation was unresolvable ('SIS.gov.eg ... review, Sept 2025'); this pass anchors presence on the ministry's own 2021 announcement and the 2024 NARSS seasonal map. EgSA (guidance lead) not verified as operationally integrated in agriculture — only NARSS confirmed.

cells.value: No operating national digital soil map/database service found — best-verified status is ABSENT for a public national digital soil information service, with legacy and research assets: FAO Soils Portal hosts legacy (digitised historical) national soil maps of Egypt; ESDAC holds the 1970s 'Soil Map of Egypt' soil survey papers; soil survey capacity sits institutionally with ARC's Soils, Water and Environment Research Institute (SWERI); an 'Egyptian digital land resources database' built by NARSS with the Ministry of Scientific Research appears in project literature without a locatable public service; digital soil mapping studies (land capability, salinity) are sub-national academic products. A salt-affected-lands distribution map was reported in Egyptian ag press (T5). Egypt-specific contribution to FAO GSP products (e.g., GSASmap national dataset) could not be confirmed this pass.
cells.source_title: FAO Soils Portal — Regional and National Soil Maps and Databases (Egypt legacy maps)
cells.quality_evidence: Institutional home exists (ARC/SWERI) but no public digital soil information portal, national soil database service, or gazetted programme for one was located. Historical national coverage exists only as legacy maps (FAO legacy collection; ESDAC 1975-era survey papers).
cells.search_trail: DATA-GAP-STYLE TRAIL (absence finding): searched FAO Soils Portal and Global Soil Partnership pages (soil maps and databases; GSASmap country contributions), ISRIC world soil geographic databases, ESDAC, ARC/SWERI (arc.sci.eg DNS-fails from test network), NARSS/CGIAR-MEL project literature, peer-reviewed Egyptian DSM studies (ScienceDirect), Arabic press for a national soil fertility map (none found beyond a salt-affected-lands map news item, T5). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Indicator definition ambiguity: legacy paper-era maps digitised by FAO arguably constitute a 'national soil map' at rung Announced/Adopted — recorded here as Absent for an operating *digital soil information service*, which is what the ladder measures; reviewer may re-anchor. arc.sci.eg unreachable internationally blocks direct verification of SWERI holdings.
cells.notes: CONSISTENT with prior desk pass ('no verified evidence of a comprehensive, publicly accessible digital national soil map/database'); divergence is presentational — prior recorded 'sector review, level 2', this pass records the absence finding explicitly with the tried-and-failed trail. GSASmap: generic FAO pages confirm 118+ contributing countries but Egypt's inclusion was not individually verifiable — do not cite Egypt as a contributor without the country list.

cells.value: No published agricultural data interoperability standards/schemas found for Egypt — ABSENT after active refutation attempt. Nearest instruments, none ag-specific: (1) Open Data Policy (NCAI, 2025, T3) mandates cross-government standardized bilingual metadata profiles and open machine-readable formats (CSV/JSON/XML) for released datasets; (2) the policy announces a forthcoming Data Governance Law, executive regulations, a data classification framework, and an Egyptian Data Governance Authority (EDGA) — 'once it is established' (not yet enacted); (3) Egypt-GovStack partnership (Nov 2022) for building-block government interoperability; (4) de facto database integration around the Farmer Card (MALR with e-finance/ABE/Meeza payment rails) operates without any published schema or standard. No MALR data dictionary, ag-data exchange standard, or sectoral schema registry was located in Arabic or English.
cells.source_title: Open Data Policy, Arab Republic of Egypt (NCAI, 2025) — closest instrument; no ag-specific standard exists
cells.quality_evidence: Not applicable at rung Absent. Context: the 2025 Open Data Policy's metadata/format mandates would apply to any future released agricultural datasets, and the announced Data Governance Law + EDGA are the likely future vehicle for sectoral data standards.
cells.search_trail: REFUTATION TRAIL: searched MCIT/Digital Egypt interoperability framework (no published e-GIF with ag schemas found), ai.gov.eg Open Data Policy full text (extracted; no ag-specific standards), GovStack Egypt partnership, trade.gov Egypt digital economy guides, Arabic search for electronic linking/unification of agricultural databases (الربط الإلكتروني/توحيد قواعد البيانات الزراعية — returned Iraq/Jordan/Saudi results, nothing Egyptian), MALR portals (moa.gov.eg, agri.gov.eg — statistics products but no standards documents). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: PREREQUISITE UC:AGI cell — the v1.6 run graded this 'Present (narrow)' on the strength of general Digital-Egypt integration; on the facts there is no published ag-data standard, so the prerequisite call depends on whether cross-government policy instruments count. Flag for Katreyna: does the Open Data Policy's generic metadata/format mandate satisfy a 'narrow presence' reading, or does this prerequisite require sector-specific schemas?
cells.notes: CONSISTENT with prior desk pass ('no dedicated agricultural-data interoperability standard identified') after an active attempt to refute it in both languages. New since prior: the 2025 Open Data Policy and the announced Data Governance Law/EDGA are concrete, citable near-term vehicles — worth re-checking next loop for enactment.

bundle_issues: 1) TEMPLATE BLEED: the cell guidance for this Egypt bundle carries Nigeria leads (NIN farmer registry, NBS/opendata.gov.ng, NiMet, NASRDA) — addressed Egypt only; confirm the orchestrator splits country leads before dispatch. 2) .EG RESOLVABILITY: Egyptian official domains are fragile from outside Egypt — sis.gov.eg serves a TLS chain WebFetch rejects (verified via curl -k), and arc.sci.eg, en.emaeg.org, nwp.gov.eg, capmas.gov.eg, censusinfo.capmas.gov.eg all DNS-failed or timed out at capture (2026-08-22), while www.ema.gov.eg, moa.gov.eg, agri.gov.eg, ai.gov.eg resolved. Protocol requires Wayback archiving only for T4-T5; recommend extending archiving to unstable T3 (.eg) deep links at capture time. 3) UN eGovKB emits malformed HTTP headers that break WebFetch — verify via curl; link resolves in browsers. 4) data.gov.eg is a named national commitment that does not yet resolve — a good tracking probe for future loops. 5) Farmer Card metrics circulate in three non-comparable units (cards, farmers, holdings) with no official series — any scored coverage ratio for 3.3 needs a Katreyna ruling on numerator/denominator. 6) ODIN 2024 Egypt (agriculture category openness scores) exists but sits behind a JS app; one manual capture would strengthen 3.5 next loop.
